t: Drawing the rig as built, and why every transducer gets a filter
s: Drawing the rig as built, and why every transducer gets a filter Jacquelyn was drawing the bioreactor for the wiki and the 12 September meeting with Prof. Sattely and Prof. Endy, and kept finding that no drawing matched the rig. On 11 September Chars drew it by hand, coloured by status. BIOREACTOR · P&ID · DECISION Chars, Jacquelyn, Joshua, Timmy Drew the piping and instrumentation diagram by hand on 11 September. Black for the current version, orange for future design, green for the biosecurity design. P is a pressure transducer, F a flow meter, D a diaphragm pump. 11 September: Chars’s hand drawing. Black current, orange future, green biosecurity 12 September: the hollow fibre module in the rig Put a Luer valve and a filter on every pressure transducer. A filter is what lets each transducer be calibrated; the prototype of early September had none, which is why its pressures could not be calibrated. Corrected the drawings line by line in the channel. Shell-side flow ran the wrong way in the first draft. ‘OD600’ became ‘in-line photometer’, ‘pH sensor’ became ‘pH probe’, every ‘pressure sensor’ became ‘pressure transducer’. The pH probe and outlet tube sit below the liquid surface; the inlet tube and air filter above it. The flow meter goes in line, because a flow meter cannot work in a dead end, and the lumen loop has only one. Prototype 1 (6 June) redrawn Prototype 2 (14 June) redrawn Prototype 3 (10 July) redrawn Made the last two fixes on 15 September while Chars soldered. A Luer valve on the left side of the pressure transducer, and the sampler moved from top right to bottom left. Prototype 4 as drawn on 14 September 15 September: the two final fixes, marked A Luer valve and a filter on every transducer Without them a transducer cannot be calibrated, and an uncalibrated reading is what the 4 September run gave us. Four transducers, one at each membrane port, so a fault can be placed. Keeping one transducer per side as in early September. It reads, but nobody can say how well. Drawings follow the rig only as far as someone checks them Redraw after every run that changes the plumbing. Run the first culture under the light plate.

t: A cheaper photometer: fibres in place of the lens and beam splitter
s: A cheaper photometer: fibres in place of the lens and beam splitter The beam splitter, the paralleling lens and the flow cuvette are nearly all of the complex photometer’s cost. Optical fibres can carry the light in parallel and split it 1:1 between sample and reference, which removes the lens, the splitter and the long light path, and makes the device more than two-thirds smaller. SIMPLIFIED PHOTOMETER · BUILD Chars, Anton, Noah, Joshua Wrote the silica calibration procedure on 13 September before building anything. Chars made it the must-do test before the next bioreactor run (SiO2_OD600_Calibration_SOP_en.pdf). The silica was already in hand. Soldered the simplified photometer’s PCB on 14 September. Chars: the PCB had to come before the nanoparticle test. Took the first silica readings on the simplified photometer on 19 September. Anton posted the data as sio2_conc_vs_od.csv. The simplified photometer in CAD: sensors on top, cuvette through the side, light on a fibre 19 September: the first silica readings as logged Keep the flow cuvette, replace the lens and splitter with fibres The cuvette is what makes in-line measurement possible. The lens and splitter are what make it expensive. Shrinking the complex design part by part. The cost sits in the optics, not the body. The fibre split is designed to correct LED drift but is untested over a long run Run it alongside the complex photometer for days, not hours. Run both photometers on one silica series.

t: First culture under the light plate, and the post snaps on the shaker
s: First culture under the light plate, and the post snaps on the shaker The LPA had lit LEDs since May and never a culture. On 19 September it ran the first one, ACC deaminase level 2, with twelve tubes across green and red at three intensities. LIGHT PLATE · FIRST CULTURE · FAILURE DIAGNOSIS Timmy, Gabriel, Chars, Alex Overnight on a shaker, a bottom-plate post broke off at its base and several wires came loose. Light also leaked through the white tube holder into neighbouring wells, which affected that run’s data. Set up twelve tubes under three green and one red intensity column. Tubes 1–3 green 100 %; 5–7 green 12 %; 9–11 green 2 %; tubes 4, 8 and 12 red at 100 %, 12 % and 2 %. 19 September: the light-control assay set up under the LPA Plate-reader OD at 2 hours Later read-out, 19 September Read OD on the plate reader at 2 hours and through the evening. The results are filed as 20260919_OptoLPA_ACCD_Run1_ODresults.xlsx. Found the damage the next morning. The shaker frequency was likely too high for the print. The post failed where it joins the plate. The housing on the shaker: debris around a torn hole in the bottom plate The snapped post, screw still through it 20 September: the last read-out of the run Do not use this run’s numbers as a light-dose result Light leaking between wells means each tube saw more than its own setting. The rebuild has to fix the leak and the mounting before the next culture. Correcting the readings for the leak afterwards. We never measured how much light crossed between wells. Light leaks between wells through the white holder Print the holder in black, with thicker walls. Base fails on the shaker Use all four screw positions and reinforce every solder joint. Rebuild the base and the holder.

t: Black holder, four screws, MOSFETs inside
s: Black holder, four screws, MOSFETs inside The rebuild after entry 30. The record gives no date for it, only that it came after the shaker failure and before the wiki’s final design in October. LIGHT PLATE · FINAL DESIGN · BUILD Anton, Noah Moved the MOSFET stage from a breadboard beside the array onto a perfboard under the LED holder, inside the housing. One MOSFET per intensity tier, each switching a green and a red column of four, driven from PWM pins 9, 10 and 11. Before: three MOSFETs on a breadboard beside the holder After: perfboard and MOSFETs beneath the LED holder Final: the black tube holder seated on the housing Used all four screw positions, up from two, and reinforced every solder joint. Printed the tube holder in black and raised its walls from 2 loops to 4. That is the fix for the light leaking between wells. The CAD, part by part: bottom plate, sliders, housing, LED holder, tube holder, perfboard FINAL DIMENSIONS From the CAD. Footprint 211 × 164 mm; 217 mm across sliders Housing height 108 mm Tube holder height +80 mm LED grid 4 × 6 on 18 mm pitch Tube bores 24 × 17 mm Fix the leak and the base in one rebuild Both failures came from the same run and both are print and assembly changes. The rebuilt base has not been back on a shaker, and no culture has run under the final design. Rebuilt base not re-tested on a shaker Run it overnight on the shaker empty first. No end-to-end culture run under the final design Repeat the 19 September assay. Power for the valves.

t: Soldering the valve power system
s: Soldering the valve power system Prototype 2 adds control: servo pinch valves at the membrane and pH dosing. On 26 September Joshua’s goal was to finish soldering the power system (電壓系統). BIOREACTOR · PROTOTYPE 2 · BUILD Joshua, Chars Finished six valves. Still to do at GEMS: the pumps and the pH probe, plus the wiki. 26 September: the soldering bench The driver board Valve wiring laid out Fixed the pinch valve hardware for the build. An STS3215 12 V servo drives each pinch valve, one near the out-lumen end of the membrane and one near the in-lumen end, each about 2 inches from the connection. Placed the pH probe in the reservoir cap, plugged into the Arduino. A small pump is designed to dose sodium hydroxide from a second bottle through a Luer valve into the out-lumen line. The printed valve bodies with their servos Servo pinch valves at both lumen ends Entry 23 chose the servo because it holds when power is cut. Two of them let the lumen side be closed off at both ends. The servo choice has still not been bench-tested for holding force (entry 23). Pinch valve design is not on record Put the valve CAD and the holding-force test on the wiki. pH dosing is designed, not run Run the NaOH pump against a falling pH. Register what the next run should do, before it runs.

t: Registering a growth-rate forecast before the run
s: Registering a growth-rate forecast before the run A model that is only ever checked against data it has already seen proves little. On 1 October, before any bioreactor run of WB800 secreting ACC deaminase, we registered what the next run’s growth rate would be, with a pass criterion, and fixed the file. BIOREACTOR · DIGITAL TWIN · DECISION Timmy, Felix, Sara Took the prior from a plate-reader fit (150 µL wells) of the same strain. The plate’s temperature was not recorded, and our 37 °C shake-flask fit is about four times faster, so the criterion does not apply to a batch run at 37 °C. REGISTERED 1 OCTOBER Only r is scored. K and X₀ were fitted on the plate-reader scale, and no cross-calibration to the in-line 2 mm cuvette exists yet. Specific growth rate r 0.2986 h⁻¹, 90 % interval 0.2705 – 0.3300 (doubling 139 min, 126 – 154) the fitted r falls inside the interval Growth curve shape logistic, prior-predicted trace NRMSE below 15 % Time to OD 0.5 7.3 h from OD 0.10; 9.8 h from 0.05; 13.0 h from 0.02 observed time inside the 5–95 % band Wrote down what each outcome would mean. If the rate fails and the shape passes, temperature is the first place to look. If both fail, the prior does not cross from plate to bioreactor, and we report that. Set up a leaf temperature and wetness sensor on the bench on 2 October. The twin’s field inputs were all online data until now. This is the first local sensor beside a crop; it is tested on its own, not yet in the loop. Register first, score on the first clean run A forecast written after the data cannot fail, so it cannot pass either. Fitting the model to the next run and reporting the fit. It would look better and test nothing. Plate and cuvette scales are not cross-calibrated Read the same culture on both before scoring K or X₀. The run with the codon-optimised strain.

t: Run 5: the reading breaks down after ten hours
s: Run 5: the reading breaks down after ten hours On 8 October we began the second full run through the bioreactor, with WB800 secreting codon-optimised ACC deaminase constitutively, at 37 °C, permeate drawn at 24 mL/min (a flux of 72 LMH). It was the first run that could score the registered forecast. BIOREACTOR · RUN 5 · FAILURE DIAGNOSIS Chloe, Joshua, Chars, Timmy 37.5 h logged over 38 h in four files, because the run was restarted three times. In-line OD rose from 0.10 to 0.30 over the first nine hours, then fell away while the culture was still there. Nothing after 10.6 h can be read as a growth curve. Historic moment!! We are beginning our second full bioreactor run through of the codon optimized ACCD. 8 October: the loop in the incubator at the start The reservoir and photometer at the start 23:34 the same night: the dashboard Posted OD and pH by hand on 9 and 10 October alongside the logger. Joshua took readings at 8:45 on 9 October and 8:58 on 10 October. 9 October 08:45: the dashboard 10 October 08:58: OD and pH CANDIDATE CAUSES · TABLE 33 Run 5 cannot score the forecast. A sixth of windows carried more than 20 % bubbles bubbles in the beam confirmed in the log Reference channel moved 4.8× across the run the optics, not the culture: the reference never passes through it confirmed in the log pH held at 6.90 for twenty hours the probe, not the culture confirmed in the log Permeate drawn too hard (72 LMH) pulls gas and stresses the loop tested in run 6 Halve the permeate flux and gate the photometer Permeate to 12 mL/min, 36 LMH. An acceptance gate on the OD channel: a window that fails its own checks holds the last accepted value and is flagged. Scoring the forecast on the first nine hours. Too short, and the reading was already failing. Bubbles reach the beam at high permeate flux Run 6 at half the flux. pH probe sticks Check it against a bench meter at the start and end of the next run. Calibrate both photometers on silica before run 6.

t: Silica calibration: both photometers on one series
s: Silica calibration: both photometers on one series TiO₂ (entry 25b) stopped at OD600 1.9 and never included the simplified photometer. On 10 October we ran silica, the iGEM standard, through the same loop with the BioDrop, the complex photometer and the simplified photometer reading every step: the first run with all three on one series. PHOTOMETERS · SiO₂ CALIBRATION · TEST Timmy, Noah, Joshua, Jacquelyn Added silica to 500 mL of 1 % SDS in 2.5 mg steps from 2.5 to 100 mg, forty points, stirred and circulated. Streamed live to a shared sheet so the team could watch. 10 October: both photometers running the final calibration The complex photometer, CAD section Preparing the next silica addition Found the BioDrop is the ceiling, not our instruments. Its direct reading returns exactly 2.50 from 70 mg. Above OD 2.5 we measured dilutions and multiplied back, and that reconstruction falls as silica is added at 7 of 20 steps, which a weighed inert standard cannot do. COMPLEX PHOTOMETER AGAINST THE BIODROP Dilution-corrected BioDrop. Up to OD 2.5 the complex photometer reads absolute OD600 with no transform. OD 0–1.0 1.001 −0.123 0.988 −0.12 OD 0–2.5 0.995 −0.074 0.982 −0.08 above 2.5 0.594 +0.944 0.796 −0.33 Got the simplified photometer linear across the whole range, but compressed. R² = 0.992 against silica mass (complex: 0.974). One linear conversion rescales it: OD = 5.573 × r − 0.073. It spans 0.03 to 0.60 against 0.05 to 3.17 for the complex photometer. SMALLEST RESOLVABLE CHANGE, AS SiO₂ MASS Point-to-point scatter divided by the change in reading per mg. The BioDrop read one hand-pipetted cuvette per point, so this compares repeatability. Complex photometer 0.010 OD 0.21 mg 0.46 mg Simplified photometer 0.004 OD 0.49 mg 0.78 mg BioDrop 0.106 OD 2.20 mg 3.60 mg Argued about why the simplified reading is a fifth of the other. Dr. Pak’s first thought was a shorter light path. Both use the same 2 mm flow cuvette, so it is not path length. Noah suspects light spreading from the fibre; Dr. Pak raised stray light. Not settled. V1 more sheer light intensity, but shaky when OD gets high. V2 lower light intensity, but more stable, and less sensitivity so might miss small turbulence. Tested eight filter estimators on the same readings, and added two gates after the median filter. A bubble that fills the cuvette for seconds makes every reading wrong yet consistent; MAD caught 94 % of partial disturbances but none of these. Gate 1 rejects a reading when MAD and an upper percentile differ by more than 0.03 OD. Gate 2 holds any step above 0.05 OD or 5 % until three readings agree. 12 October: the newer photometer, light almost against the cuvette The Uno Q breakout wiring both photometers share Complex photometer in the reactor, simplified where cost matters The complex photometer reads OD600 directly to 2.5, resolves changes twice as fine, and its reference beam stops slow LED drift being logged as growth. The simplified one is linear and cheaper, but needs its 5.57× factor and resolves half as finely. One run on one mineral standard. Silica and bacteria do not scatter identically. Why the simplified reading is compressed is unexplained Sit down with Dr. Pak with the hardware, and test stray light directly. Both photometers untested on known cell densities Repeat the series with B. subtilis. Run 6, with the gate running.

Anton revised the rack model and asked Chars to check it on 9 October. Only one shell-side outlet is open, the one at the top of the module on the lumen-outlet side. The bottom shell outlet has a Luer valve on it, closed and connected to nothing yet. t: Run 6: a clean curve, and the forecast passes
s: Run 6: a clean curve, and the forecast passes Same strain as run 5, with two changes: permeate halved to 12 mL/min (36 LMH) and the photometer acceptance gate running. Pass condition, registered on 1 October: fitted growth rate inside 0.2705 to 0.3300 h⁻¹. BIOREACTOR · RUN 6 · TEST Chars, Joshua, Timmy, Noah Top: OD600 windows the gate accepted. Bottom: the pressure the module needs beyond what its geometry needs for clean water. Plotted from record_20261014_105625.csv and record_20261015_110749.csv. Ran 41.8 hours with no restart, 14 to 16 October. The gate turned away 31 of 1,083 windows. No window carried more than 20 % bubbles and the reference held within 17 %. Got a clean trace from 0.14 to 2.71. 0.14 at the first window, 1.01 at 7 h, 2.71 at 37 h. After that the sample channel fell to a tenth of the reference and the reading stepped to about 9.9 and stayed there, flagged as low signal. Scored the registered forecast. r = 0.286 ± 0.010 h⁻¹ (doubling 145 min), R² 0.978 on quarter-hourly medians from 1.5 to 6.5 h. Inside the interval. REGISTERED AGAINST RUN 6 Growth rate r 0.2986, interval 0.2705–0.3300 h⁻¹ 0.286 ± 0.010 h⁻¹ inside Curve shape logistic, NRMSE < 15 % misses the first 7 h by 30 %; passes the prior’s ceiling of 1.005 before 7 h not scored Time to OD 0.5 6.1 h from 0.14 3.6 h not scored Logged a fouling trend for the first time. Excess pressure rose from 2.0 to 3.8 kPa over 42 hours. The two spikes the Digital Twin names, at 1.1 h and 24.3 h, read zero on the permeate while the feed rises: the permeate side being opened, not the membrane. A third single window near 18.4 h reads 9.4 kPa and carries a low-reference flag. pH fell from 6.93 to 6.41 over seventeen hours, then stepped back to 7.0 inside one window. The log does not explain the step. Passed on the one scored endpoint The rate fitted to run 6 sits inside the interval registered thirteen days before it. Over those five hours a straight line fits the readings with half the residual sum of squares of the exponential, so the rate comes from a stretch where the two shapes cannot be told apart. Run 6’s pressures sit at the same magnitude as run 4’s, so they appear to carry the firmware scaling problem in entry 34a. The photometer loses the sample beam above OD about 2.7 A shorter path or a dilution loop for the top of the range. Unexplained pH step Log the probe temperature and check the probe against a bench meter. No membrane breach test on record Induce a leak deliberately and see whether the transducers flag it. Settle the parts list before anything else is published.

t: Auditing the parts list, and finding the pressure scaling wrong
s: Auditing the parts list, and finding the pressure scaling wrong The hardware material list of 7 October was complete but unpublishable: eleven internal contradictions, two of them live on the wiki. On 14 October the instructors ruled on each, the same exercise as the spec freeze of 4 July (entry 15a).
